lruCache.caption.base: An LRU cache shares one set of nodes between a hash map (key → node) and a doubly linked list (recency order) — every call drags a node to the MRU end, and on overflow the LRU end vanishes from both areas at once.
lruCache.caption.evict: Over capacity — {key} at the LRU end disappears from both areas together.
lruCache.caption.getHit: {key} was dragged to the MRU end — even a get rotates the list.
lruCache.caption.getMiss: {key} is not in the cache — the list stays as it was.
lruCache.caption.handover: Your turn — type a key and value, then press get or put.
lruCache.caption.invalidKey: {op}: only short alphanumeric keys (values) are accepted — got "{raw}"
lruCache.caption.putInsert: New key {key} entered at the MRU end (room to spare).
lruCache.caption.putUpdate: The value for {key} was updated and dragged to the MRU end.
lruCache.label.references: See also: NeetCode 146 · dev.to LRU illustrated · GeeksforGeeks LRU
lruCache.narrative.line1: An LRU cache carves a "recency order" onto a plain key-value store.
lruCache.narrative.line2: The hash slots on top give fast key → node pointer lookup,
lruCache.narrative.line3: while the doubly linked list below carries the order of use.
lruCache.narrative.line4: Both areas share the same nodes, so every call updates the two at once.
lruCache.narrative.line5: Even a get is a write in effect — it drags its node to the MRU end.
lruCache.narrative.line6: A put on a full cache makes the node at the LRU end vanish from both areas together.
stack.caption.base: A stack hands back the most recently added element first — every change happens at one single place, the top.
stack.caption.feedInput: Boxes are waiting on the input track — they will be stacked on top one by one.
stack.caption.handover: Your turn — type a value and press Push, Pop or Peek.
stack.caption.peek: Looked at the top value — the pile is unchanged.
stack.caption.push: Placed a new box on top — {value}
stack.caption.underflow: No box left to take off.
